Title: Wonders at the Winter Camp
Content: “Good morning, Winnie,” said Mom, beaming. “Do you see what I see?”
At the kitchen window, a clear `text(December)` morning greeted me with a bright sky. Mom and I did a little happy dance together.
For `text(months)` our family had been planning a `text(winter)` camping trip. We had timed the trip to coincide with the Geminids meteor shower peak, and today was finally the `text(day)`!
By `text(noon)`, we were setting up our campsite. We spent a perfect afternoon hiking and exploring until hunger drew us back to camp. Dad warmed a kettle of beef stew over the fire grate.
At bedtime we dressed in thick layers and crawled into our sleeping bags. It was cozy. “I don’t want to miss the meteors, Mom,” I said. “Are you sure you can wake up in time?”
“Don’t worry, I’ve set my watch alarm,” she replied. “`text(Two o’clock A.M.)`” Tired from the fresh cold air, a hike, and the hearty stew, we all fell off to sleep quickly.
Groggily I heard the sound, at `text(first)` as if from a long way off, then insistently, right in my ear. Mom’s alarm.
“`text(Two o’clock)`, everyone,” Mom said, softly. “Time to bundle up and head outside for the show!”
I heard Dad groan, but he made no move to get up.
I was so warm, and it was so dark and cold outside. I was just about to join Dad back in dreamland, when I saw Mom’s face in the beam of her flashlight. She looked disappointed.
“Coming, Mom,” I said as cheerfully as I could. Mom smiled. Quickly, I dressed myself in my coat, snow pants, boots, hat, and gloves.
We unzipped the tent and crawled out. When we stood up and looked around, the night world was dark as ink. Above, the sky was sprinkled with twinkling stars.
We sat on a log in our clearing, and Mom turned off the flashlight. Soon, it was as if another layer of stars filled in the spaces our light had just occupied.
And then, ZIP, a streak flashed across the sky, and another, and another.
“WOW!” we said in unison. Streak after streak bombarded the sky. It was nature’s fireworks display, better than anything we could see on the `text(Fourth of July)`.
“Oh my gosh, Mom!” I exclaimed. “I am so glad I did not miss this. I’ll never forget this night as long as I live!”
Mom put her arm around me and hugged me close. I hugged her back as we continued to gaze upward at the light show.
